title: Yankees, Padres, White Sox all advance; Phillies-Braves to play do-or-die Wild Card Game 3
description: On this episode of the Baseball Bar-B-Cast, Jake and Jordan recap all the action from the Wild Card round and preview a series-deciding Game 3 between the Phillies and the Braves.
fullText:
As quickly as the Wild Card round began, it has already ended the season for three teams. With the New York Yankees, San Diego Padres and Chicago White Sox all taking care of business in the first two games, there's only one best-of-three series left, and it will decide who takes on the defending back-to-back World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers.

On this episode of the Baseball Bar-B-Cast, Jake Mintz and Jordan Shusterman recap everything that has happened in the Wild Card round so far, including the wild conclusion to the Philadelphia Phillies and Atlanta Braves' Game 2, where Bryce Harper atoned for his error in the field with a dramatic game-tying home run. They also highlight Alec Bohm's go-ahead homer that helped seal the deal for a series-deciding Game 3 on Thursday night.

Later in the show, Jake and Jordan get into the Yankees defeating archrivals the Boston Red Sox in the Bronx, which sent the Bombers back to the ALDS to face off with AL East rival Tampa Bay Rays. Then, they recap the very disappointing showing from the Houston Astros, as they were eliminated by the Chicago White Sox, as well as try to figure out where the Chicago Cubs go from here after being knocked out by the San Diego Padres in two games.

title: Ryan Spooner Hangs Up Skates After 41-Goal Bruins Run
description: Ryan Spooner retires from hockey. The former Bruin scored 41 goals in Boston. See the stats and why his quiet leadership mattered most.
fullText:
The party is over for Ryan Spooner. The former Boston Bruins forward officially announced his retirement on Tuesday after playing his final season in Slovakia. He walked away from the game after a long journey that started with a second-round pick in 2010. Spooner never became the superstar some expected, but he left a mark that goes beyond just the numbers. He scored 41 goals for Boston and played 253 games in the black and gold.

Spooner's career was a roller coaster of trades. He went from the Bruins to the Rangers, then to the Oilers, and finally the Canucks before heading overseas. He played in the KHL and Swiss leagues for years after leaving the NHL. His best season away from Boston came in 2023-24 with Omsk Avangard, where he netted 23 goals. But the real story isn't about the stats he piled up in Russia. It is about how he acted when he was a backup in Boston.

Marco Sturm, the current head coach, worked closely with Spooner's teammate Joonas Korpisalo and shared high praise for the quiet players in the locker room. According to a report by Jack Studley on X, Sturm said of Korpisalo's style, which mirrored Spooner's: "What I didn't know at first, because he was that quiet, how popular he was in the room. I give him a lot of credit by not just being a good backup, but also being a good teammate."

That kind of leadership is rare. You do not see it every day in a tough hockey town. Spooner was the guy who showed up every single day and did his job without needing the spotlight. He made the guys around him better just by being there. That is worth more than a single goal.

Let's look at the hard facts from his time in Boston. Spooner had 101 assists to go with his 41 goals for a total of 142 points. He also logged 143 hits and blocked 61 shots. These are not the numbers of a lazy player. They belong to someone who fought for every inch of ice. He even played in the 2017 playoffs, recording two assists in four games.

The end of his career came quickly after a short stint with HK Dukla Trencin. He played five games this season before hanging up the skates. In a press release translated by Google, Spooner thanked the fans and said ending his career was not an easy decision. He believed he could play one more season but felt it was the right time to stop. That honesty is refreshing in a sport full of excuses.

The Bruins need more guys like him now. The team just saw Fraser Minten score his first goal of the 2026-27 season to beat the Rangers, a game where the team won 11 straight at home to start the year. Minten signed a seven-year, $50 million deal this summer. But money does not buy the grit Spooner showed. The new roster has talent, but it needs that quiet, hard-working spirit to win in the playoffs.

Spooner's legacy is simple. He was a good teammate who gave everything he had. The Bruins won't forget the 41 goals, but they will miss the guy who made the room better.

As the Boston Red Sox's 2026 season ended with a two-game sweep by the New York Yankees in the American League Wild Card Series, veteran catcher Willson Contreras made his frustration with the organization's data-driven approach clear after Wednesday's loss.

Contreras had momentarily given Boston a glimmer of hope in the sixth inning when he launched a Statcast-projected 387-foot solo home run to right-center with two outs. The blast ended a 26-inning postseason scoring drought for the Red Sox dating back to Game 2 of last year's Wild Card Series, also against the Yankees. However, New York answered with six runs in the bottom of the inning, turning the game into a 9-2 defeat.

Boston was outscored 18-2 across the two games and was eliminated before getting a chance to play in October. The loss also extended the Red Sox's streak to five consecutive seasons without postseason baseball at Fenway Park.

After the game, Contreras was asked about manager Chad Tracy's decision to remove starter Sonny Gray in the fifth inning. Gray had allowed six hits across 4 2/3 innings and surrendered only one run, a solo homer by Luis García Jr. He left after reaching 70 pitches with runners on the corners and two outs.

Tracy replaced Gray with left-handed reliever Erik Miller to face Cody Bellinger. Miller surrendered a run-scoring single to Bellinger before allowing another single to García. Gray had recorded a .180/.235/.280 slash line against hitters during their third time facing him this season, while Bellinger had been better against left-handed pitching than right-handed pitching. Contreras responded to the question about Gray by pretending to zip his mouth closed.

He was more direct when discussing Boston's broader reliance on data and technology.

"It's not enough when you have talent, or you have data, or you have computers telling you what to do, because this is baseball," said Contreras. "The data is here to help us but at the end of the day, you're going to need experience and veteran guys to win games. There's a lot of stuff that I would like to say, but I'll state it like that."

— Foul Territory (@FoulTerritoryTV) October 1, 2026

The comments came after the Red Sox's disappointing postseason exit and a regular season that featured major swings in performance. Boston fell into a 32-46 hole before going 32-5 from June 25 through August 7, including a franchise-tying 15-game winning streak.

The team then slumped during the final month amid injuries and offensive problems, which carried into the postseason. The Red Sox's bullpen also labored through a second consecutive difficult night against New York, while Garrett Crochet's return from shoulder and lat issues lasted less than an inning. Making his first appearance since April 25, Crochet failed to record an out and was charged with four runs.

Contreras' comments only added to the fallout from an elimination that exposed disagreements over Boston's decision-making and approach under chief baseball officer Craig Breslow.

title: Troubled Gateshead fail to pay September wages
description: Gateshead's players and staff do not receive their September wages on time in the same week major funding is withdrawn from the club.
fullText:
Troubled National League side Gateshead have failed to pay players and staff their wages for September.

The club are bottom of the league and have lost their past five games, conceding 16 goals and scoring just once.

Earlier this week, Mark Nellist resigned from the board of directors and withdrew his funding support, citing that the Tyneside club was "not heading in the direction I would have liked or hoped for".

But the Heed's interim chairman Graham Wood said he was hopeful of quickly finding new investment for the club.

"Following Mark Nellist's sudden decision to withdraw his funding support for the club we have been fully focused on seeking new investment," he said.

"Significant progress has been made in the past 24 hours and we are hopeful of making an announcement in the next day or so.

"Meanwhile, to facilitate our efforts, Mark has agreed to make his shares available for a nominal sum."

title: Why penalty for Williamson handball was correct call
description: Arsenal defender Leah Williamson was at the heart of a bizarre incident in their Women's Champions League draw with Paris FC.
fullText:
A bizarre error from Arsenal defender Leah Williamson proved costly in their 2-2 draw with Paris FC on Wednesday in the Women's Champions League.

With the Gunners leading 2-1 late on, England captain Williamson stopped a short goal-kick with her hand - believing it had not been taken and that she was to take it - resulting in a penalty being awarded to the hosts, converted by Maeline Mendy.

The unusual incident means the Gunners are fourth in the Champions League table after their opening two games, but would have been second with a victory in the French capital.

After the ball had gone out of play for a goal-kick, Arsenal goalkeeper Misa Rodriguez played a quick, short pass to Williamson.

Williamson had her arm stretched out to stop the ball and place it so that she could take the goal-kick herself.

With the ball being still and on the field of play when Rodriguez played the ball to Williamson, that was deemed to be the goal-kick instead of Williamson's attempt.

Therefore Williamson was penalised for handball and Mendy levelled the match from the penalty spot.

While Arsenal felt aggrieved at the decision, the guidance on such incidents state that the decision to award a penalty was correct.

Guidance from Law 16 of the International Football Association Board's (Ifab) laws of the game state: "In goal-kick restarts, if the ball is stationary within the goal area and is kicked by any defending player, the goal-kick is considered to have been taken.

"If, after the ball is in play, [a player] commits a handball offence, a penalty kick is awarded if the offence occurred inside the kicker's penalty area.

Law 12 from Ifab also states: "It is an offence if a player deliberately touches the ball with their hand/arm."

In November 2024, Aston Villa defender Tyrone Mings committed an identical error in a Champions League match against Club Brugge.

Brugge won a penalty that was scored by Hans Vanaken, with the Belgian side winning the match 1-0.

"The biggest mistake I witnessed in my career," said Villa boss Unai Emery at the time.

Earlier that year, Gunners centre-back Gabriel also made the mistake in a Champions League match against Bayern Munich.

However in that instance, Arsenal were given the chance to retake the goal-kick.

"He [Gabriel] touched the ball with the hand because he thought it was not in game, but it was in game and the referee admitted it was in game and was handball," said then Bayern boss Thomas Tuchel.

The now England head coach also said that the error in not awarding Bayern a penalty was a "kid's mistake".

Arsenal's assistant coach Aaron D'Antino conducted post-match media duties and explained that, while the intention was for Williamson to take the goal-kick, they will use the incident as a learning experience.

"If we're looking at what we can control, it's just passing the ball to Leah from what I remember seeing. The ball was still rolling and she [Rodriguez] was moving it to Leah for her to take the goal-kicks as we normally do," said D'Antino.

"So maybe the learning in that is how we get the ball to Leah, so we don't put ourselves in that situation."

Former Arsenal and Scotland defender Jen Beattie felt the referee Iuliana Demetrescu got the decision wrong, despite the correct applications of the laws.

"For me, I just don't even know how that happens. Leah knows it's a goal-kick, she's catching the ball. That's shocking from the referee," Beattie told Paramount+.

"I would have been fuming and I would have been embarrassed if they gave that. This is not what they're trying to do. It's just beyond frustrating that that's how they've tied the game.

"Leah's obviously going [to do that] because she's going to take the goal-kick, not because she's worried about the press or trying to change it - or panicking in any situation. Leah Williamson doesn't panic in those moments, she knows what she's doing. The goalkeeper knows what she's doing as well.

"The referee has miscalled it."

title: 2027 NFL Draft stock watch features 11 players on the rise
description: Who are the biggest risers in the 2027 NFL Draft so far? Two quarterbacks have helped their stock significantly with their early showings.
fullText:
As some of the marquee 2027 NFL Draft prospects have faltered in the first month of the season, other players have capitalized on the opportunity to raise their profile.

The group of prospects expected to join the pros next April features a good amount of established stars, from quarterbacks Arch Manning and Dante Moore to wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, among others. But while Smith has continued to set college football ablaze in what is almost assuredly his final campaign, the early results have been decidedly more mixed for several of his peers.

Nevertheless, September often marks the start of a steady ascent in the draft for several players. This year is no different, with a group of standouts already on the upswing.

Here's a closer look at 11 players whose early play has earned them the label of draft risers in the opening stretch of the fall:

An undersized passer who will be 25 before his rookie season and started off in Division II would typically seem like an odd figure to factor heavily into one of the most highly anticipated quarterback classes in years. Indeed, Chambliss still amounted to something of a side attraction entering this year. In continuing his full-on star turn, though, the 6-0, 208-pound passer could force teams to have some uncomfortable reconsiderations of when the circumstances are right to break from protocol and pursue an outlier. Despite playing a brutal early slate, Chambliss has racked up 12 touchdowns and carried Mississippi, proving he can excel even without Lane Kiffin's touch. Not all of his playmaking skills will translate to the NFL, but in a league where offenses place a premium on big gains, coaching staffs should covet Chambliss' calculated aggressiveness both from within and out of structure. His resiliency and decisiveness are also major strong suits. Now firmly out of range for being considered merely a developmental option or an entertaining backup, Chambliss is sure to test the creativity and adaptability of front offices as the pre-draft process continues.

Stats can hardly tell a complete story for any college quarterback, especially in a small sample size that hasn't entailed facing top competition. Still, it's impossible not to take notice of Mensah's masterful start in Miami, during which he's thrown more touchdowns (14) than incompletions (12). Exhibiting command and poise is essential for the Tulane and Duke transfer, who only has pedestrian physical tools when compared to some of the other more gifted throwers in this class. Mensah will also have to show more comfort working down the field and to the sidelines after primarily attacking short - and an understandable way to weaponize Malachi Toney - and over the middle. But if he continues to make great strides with his processing and decision-making against much firmer competition, he'll spark some compelling conversations about his placement in the quarterback pecking order.

With Baugh, Mississippi's Kewan Lacy and Missouri's Ahmad Hardy all putting forth compelling cases entering the season, the battle to be the first running back selected in 2027 figured to make for a fierce competition. Baugh, however, has seemingly cut that debate short. Through four games, he's been borderline unstoppable, rushing for a Football Bowl Subdivision-high 600 yards and 11 touchdowns. The 6-1, 225-pound ball carrier already had all the trappings of a workhorse back. This fall, though, he's ripped off a run of 50 yards or 

Chambliss might be the catalyst for Mississippi's attack, but electric pass catchers are required to make the most of the quarterback's daring tendencies. Having risen from an integral part of a robust receiver room to the focal point of the passing attack, Alexander is more than doing his part to make good on Chambliss' deep-ball prowess. The former Wake Forest transfer has racked up 429 yards - the second most in the Southeastern Conference - and four touchdowns in four games. His background as a high school track standout in Georgia is readily evident on every snap, as he's particularly adept at getting corners to bite at the faintest sign of a fake or hesitation before racing past them downfield. The 6-0, 180-pound target might need to fill out his frame a bit more and demonstrate he can consistently conquer press coverage, but his game-breaking potential should have him rocketing up draft boards.

With Jordyn Tyson off to the Saints, the Sun Devils reloaded at receiver by inking two major transfers in Harris and Omarion Miller. The latter figured to be the more consequential move for next year's draft, but the former is making a far bigger splash early in the season. Harris has accounted for 374 receiving yards - nearly half of his team's total output - along with five touchdown catches. His deep-threat credentials had already been established at Boston College, but the 6-5, 220-pound pass catcher is reinforcing his field-stretching skills by averaging 17.4 yards per reception. In a receiver class that lacks much clarity beyond the top trio of Smith, Coleman and Becker, Harris has mounted a push for a spot in the top 50 - and possibly consideration even earlier.

Does college football have a sufficient supply of talented tight ends to satisfy the NFL's uptick in demand at the position? Beyond Oregon's Jamari Johnson and LSU's Trey'Dez Green, this year's group doesn't seem to measure up to the one teams flocked to in April. The emergence of Reynolds, however, has helped quell some concerns about depth in the upcoming draft. As one of a horde of former Penn State players who followed James Franklin to Virginia Tech, the former five-star recruit has found his footing in a new setting, needing just four games to set career highs with 30 catches, 280 yards and four touchdowns. The 6-4, 250-pound target can't measure up to Johnson or Green as an athletic marvel, but he's nimble enough to free himself from coverage and pick up additional yards after the catch. And with his comfort working as an inline blocker, Reynolds should be an attractive option for a team looking to round out and diversify its offense.

With bookend offensive tackles Francis Mauigoa and Markel Bell both departing as early NFL draft picks, Miami could have been forgiven if it struggled with pass protection in the early going this season. Okunlola ensured that didn't happen. The 6-6, 330-pound blocker stepped in at left tackle and has been superlative from the start, helping keep Mensah as part of a front that has allowed just three total sacks on 136 total dropbacks thus far. Some more refinement would serve the first-year starter well, but a former five-star recruit who was nicknamed "The Pancake Honcho" shouldn't require a hard sell for teams if he keeps playing like this.

Put Johnson anywhere along the front and he's bound to excel. The third-year starter has played at every spot except right guard during his time at Minnesota and made another switch last week, moving back to center from left guard. The result: The 6-6, 325-pound blocker was named the Outland Trophy National Player of the Week. Though his best work has come as a forceful presence in the ground game, Johnson has also helped put statuesque pocket passer Drake Lindsey at ease. Considered by some as a fringe first-round prospect entering the year - he checked in at No. 28 to the Bills in my preseason mock draft - Johnson now might be firmly in Day 1 territory.

It should come as little surprise that a former basketball standout who played just one year of high school football might need some time before fully coming into his own against top college competition. Thompkins showed promise in stretches in 2024-25 after playing in just three games during his first two years at USC, but he's taken his game to a distinct new level after transferring to Alabama. Through four games, he's already matched his previous career high with three sacks on the season. Thompkins is far more nimble and explosive than one might expect of a 6-5, 300-pound defensive linemen. He might not be a fit for every team given his body type and skill set, but he could be a considerably disruptive force as a 3-4 defensive end or defensive tackle in a defense that allows him to get upfield.

With offenses across the NFL shifting back to more under-center looks, it might not be long before teams scramble to add hyperathletic linebackers as a necessary countermeasure for the schematic swing. Cole might be exactly what those defenses are in search of. The 6-3, 235-pounder already demonstrated his ample pursuit speed and bend last season, when he led the Bulldogs with 4 1/2 sacks as a backup. Now, however, he's getting to showcase the full extent of his abilities, as his size and fluidity allow him to stick with running backs and tight ends in coverage or chase down ball carriers to either sideline. He also served up a reminder of just how uniquely explosive he is for his position when he scooped up Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer's fumble and raced 85 yards to the end zone with it, pulling away from his opponents like a wide receiver breaking free from an overmatched corner.

In snagging five interceptions in his first three games, Lopa, the 6-5, 210-pound safety, has stepped to the forefront as one of college football's most scintillating young defensive playmakers. The Oregon transfer is still in need of some seasoning after playing sparingly in his first two years with the Ducks. His tackling, in particular, isn't yet up to par, as he can struggle when forced to come to balance and finish off plays even when he's in position to do so. But defensive backs with his size, movement ability and ball skills are rare, and teams are sure to be drawn to what he can offer as a versatile piece in coverage.

title: Real Madrid superstar’s post-injury vacation approved by Mourinho and the club – report
description: Real Madrid ace Kylian Mbappe escaped with a minor injury in France’s first game of the international break and was relieved from national team duty immediately by the manager Zinedine Zidane.The cu...
fullText:
Real Madrid ace Kylian Mbappe escaped with a minor injury in France's first game of the international break and was relieved from national team duty immediately by the manager Zinedine Zidane.

The current diagnosis is of a posterior capsule hyperextension of the left knee, and his recovery time is estimated to be in weeks.

Yet, it could well have been much worse and it is said that the player may well have required surgery if he had played longer.

Currently, the player continues to be in France and has not returned to Madrid.

He has been spotted with his friends and his partner, and it has unsurprisingly led to a lot of speculation on why he is on vacation when he should be working on his return.

Mourinho has backed Mbappe's time off. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

As confirmed by AS in a recent update, however, Mbappe's trip to his country and the time he is enjoying off with his partner and friends is not secretive. In fact, the club completely backed his vacation.

Jose Mourinho is aware of the player taking some time off in France, as are the coaching staff and the medical team of the club.

They all understand that Mbappe's setback only requires rest and that the player returning to the Valdebebas may serve no real purpose.

His recovery plan, in that sense, is said to be 'co-ordinated' and 'consensual' as they describe it in the club offices.

The idea is that he will take his recovery slow and pace it out, likely even missing the team's first game after the break.

Having Mbappe fit for the Clasico is the priority. (Photo by Yasser Bakhsh/Getty Images)

Real Madrid's first game after the break is against Villarreal, and Mourinho and Co. prioritise the player being available in the long run over him being fit for the game against the Yellow Submarines.

The goal, quite clearly, is to have Mbappe fit and raring for the game against Barcelona later in October and the management considers his presence on that night to be fundamental.

So far, the Frenchman has been Real Madrid's top finishing presence in the opposition box and has carried Real Madrid's attack alongside Jude Bellingham.

The sensible idea, in that sense, would be to keep him fit and ready for the big games against Roma, Barcelona and RB Leipzig.

title: Bills react to tough start for Patriots QB Drake Maye
description: Buffalo Bills DC Jim Leonhard, New England Patriots QB Drake Maye on division matchup
fullText:
The Bills open division play Sunday against a quarterback off to the worst stretch of his career, and defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard is treating him like a problem anyway.

Buffalo's coaching staff met with reporters Monday to close the book on the Week 3 win over the Los Angeles Chargers and turn the page to the first divisional game of the season against the New England Patriots. The biggest topic was New England quarterback Drake Maye, who makes for a "tricky" evaluation this week, per Leonhard.

Maye was in the MVP conversation last season, ranking third in passing touchdowns (31), leading the NFL in passer rating (113.5), completion percentage (72%) and finished tied for lead in win percentage (.824). This against what many considered to be an easy schedule, before getting cooked by the Seattle Seahawks in the Super Bowl.

He has since thrown one touchdown pass against six interceptions and been sacked nine times through three games. That is a far cry from the player Leonhard spent late January getting ready to face in the AFC Championship.

"You turn on the tape from last year, and it was dynamic," the Bills DC said. "We played him in Denver, obviously at the end of the year, and you got to see the best version of what he was going into that game."

Last season, Maye threw for nearly 4,400 yards with 31 passing touchdowns and four rushing scores while carrying the Patriots to an AFC East title and a Super Bowl appearance. The playoffs went the other way: Denver held him without a touchdown and dropped him five times in the AFC Championship, and Seattle picked him off twice while sacking him six more times in the Super Bowl.

He sees the matchup against Buffalo as an opportunity to right the ship.

"This is an opportunity to band together and realize that the best football that we play is together and realizing that starts with me with protecting the football and protecting this team," Maye said. "That's my job, and I've been failing to do that."

Leonhard called Maye's postseason slide — four interceptions and 21 sacks across four games — "slip ups" next to "MVP level" regular-season film, and the struggles have bled into 2026. Maye and the Patriots arrive in Buffalo with the league's lowest-scoring offense at 12.0 points per game.

"You're watching a guy now that's you can tell he's going through some stuff and struggling a little bit, but at the same time he drops back and hits his top step and lets one rip and it's an explosive play," he added.

"You just have to put some pressure on him and hope that the trend continues. Great players are eventually going to come out the other side. You just hope it's after you play them."

The Bills head coach shared his thoughts on facing the Patriots QB with the press today as well.

"It is a week to week-to-week league, and it is so hard to play the position," Joe Brady said. "Drake Maye, he's an outstanding quarterback, he's played for so long at such a high level, he is going to present so many issues for us this week."

Justin Jefferson is arguably the best wide receiver in the NFL, but the former first-round pick suffered an ankle injury against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and could not return to the game. The fifth wide receiver taken in the 2025 NFL Draft, Justin Jefferson quickly established himself as one of the biggest steals in his draft class. Appearing in all 16 games while making 14 starts, the rookie finished his inaugural campaign with 88 receptions for 1,400 yards and seven touchdowns.

He continued to dominate from there, earning First-Team All-Pro honors on two separate occasions while leading the league in receptions (128) and yards (1,809) in 2022. The 2025 season was a relative down year as he struggled to develop a rapport with quarterback J.J. McCarthy, but he still ended the season with 84 receptions for 1,048 yards and two touchdowns. While Justin Jefferson looked like his old self in the first two weeks of the season, he suffered an ankle injury early in Week 3 and could not return to the field. While this won't be a long-term injury, the superstar wideout did not practice yesterday and could miss Week 4's contest against the Miami Dolphins.

It's hard to overstate just how unfortunate a serious Justin Jefferson injury would be for the Minnesota Vikings, and how lucky the team is that this isn't a long-term issue. Even with the star wide receiver in the lineup, Minnesota's passing attack hasn't looked all too dominant thus far in the season. Starting quarterback Kyler Murray suffered a concussion early in Week 1, forcing journeyman Carson Wentz to finish the contest and start Week 2. While Murray returned to the lineup in Week 3, he didn't look all too impressive. Playing most of the contest without Justin Jefferson, the quarterback completed just 15 of his 29 attempts for 168 yards, one touchdown, and one interception.

The Minnesota Vikings are a worse team without Justin Jefferson in the lineup, but they probably won't need him to win in Week 4. The Miami Dolphins are perhaps the worst team in football, and Jefferson probably won't be the difference between a win and a loss. There is no such thing as an easy win in the NFL, but Minnesota is considerably more talented and should comfortably win this contest.

title: Russell says his 'confidence is back and growing'
description: George Russell says he "doesn't feel lost any more" as he seeks to end a difficult season on a high and chase down team-mate Kimi Antonelli's championship lead.
fullText:
George Russell says he "doesn't feel lost any more" as he seeks to end a difficult season on a high and chase down team-mate Kimi Antonelli's championship lead.

Russell won his third race of the season in Azerbaijan last weekend, and his first for three months, and says he has made a breakthrough in terms of understanding how to drive the Mercedes car.

The Briton trails Antonelli by 66 points in the championship with either seven or eight races still remaining.

"The thing that's changed is I feel my performances are strong enough to fight for victory week in week out," Russell said.

"I know what I need from the car and myself and I don't really feel lost any more.

"Confidence is back and it's growing again and it's all coming a bit more naturally, which is how it has been for most of my career and not how it's been for most of the season."

Mercedes are expecting a strong challenge from McLaren at the flowing Sepang track this weekend as its characteristics should suit the world champions' car.

But the team have their first major upgrade for some time and hope that will bring them into contention.

Asked whether another strong performance at this weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia could change the psychology of the title fight, Russell said: "I've never really felt in a position to fight for the victories because my performances weren't strong enough.

"But now finally I feel I'm in a place I can fight for victory week in week out.

"Of course there is a big deficit in the championship, but there is a third of a season to go and still so much can happen. I am just going to go race by race. I feel more at one with the car and hopefully this upgrade will play into my favour a bit more. So bring it on."

Russell started the season as championship favourite but Antonelli took control early on as Russell struggled to get to grips with the Mercedes designed for this year's all-new car and engine rules.

He has had to "consciously adjust" his driving style.

"I went through a few races where I was having to think how to make those adjustments, whereas now it's all just a bit more intuitive and a bit more natural," Russell said.

"So what I set out to achieve, in terms of getting the car [into] a slightly better window, I'm now achieving without having to think about it as much. So I can just focus on driving fast."

Antonelli had a difficult weekend in Baku, with a crash in qualifying leaving him 16th on the grid, from where he recovered to finished fifth.

The Italian said: "Last weekend was probably there worst weekend from me of the season.

"But still good learning from the weekend and was also a very strange race for me in Baku because it was one of those races where I consciously tried not to take any risks and just drive under the limit which was very weird but it was what I needed on Sunday. I needed a clean result after a very disrupted weekend.

"I wasn't happy after the race but I learned the most important learning was I need to be always 100% because if I don't try to do everything right in my power then nothing is going to come my way."

Lewis Hamilton has declared Frederic Vasseur as "the guy to lead us" two days after Ferrari made an unusual public statement backing their team principal after speculation over this position.

The seven-time champion, who is third in the drivers' title race while Ferrari are second in the constructors' battle, said removing Vasseur would be a mistake.

"He's doing a fantastic job," Hamilton said. If you look at the history, how many people [have been swapped] out [of] that role… and I feel like it's in a better place than it's been before.

"But it's not a one-man situation. It's lots and lots of people coming together and if you want to point fingers, point it somewhere else. There's people above who are also part of it.

"Fred's in his position, he's not going anywhere and I'm here to stay with him and I still believe fully in where we're going.

"Swapping him out won't change how the team is moving forward. If anything it will be detrimental."

Hamilton pointed to the progress Ferrari have made since a winless 2025 season, in which they finished fourth in the teams' championship. He and Leclerc have each won a race this year.

Ferrari started the season with the best chassis in terms of cornering performance, but their engine has fallen short of those produced by Mercedes and Red Bull.

Hamilton said: "We're second in the championship, a huge improvement on last year already. And that's with a deficit on power of average 0.4secs [per lap] every single weekend. Some races it's 0.6sec and we've still be delivering really great performances.

"And that just highlights how great a job people at the factory have done. All the negativity takes away from that.

"Of course we're not where we want to be but you don't go from last year's experience straight to number one. It's a process and I think we've built a good foundation this year, we need to continue to build on it. We're not perfect yet but I do believe we can get there.

I think we've had the best car this year. But it's unfortunate we have been down 0.4secs on power. That is difficult overcome but it's something we're working on for next year."

title: J.J. McCarthy hits the ground running with New York Giants
description: Quarterback J.J. McCarthy has been with the New York Giants for mere days, but he's already staying late and getting up to speed.
fullText:
It didn't take long for quarterback J.J. McCarthy to hit the ground running with his new team, the New York Giants, after coming over in a trade with the Minnesota Vikings on Monday.

"I mean, it's been good to get him here. I'm excited about it," head coach John Harbaugh told reporters about McCarthy's arrival on Wednesday. "It's an opportunity for us to improve our team, one little way maybe. And who knows where it goes or where it doesn't go.

"But yeah, I've seen a guy. I mean, he had a really good practice. Seems like he picked things up we asked him to pick up really well. Was in here late, early. Studying, learning. Has a really good football foundation, all that kind of stuff. And that's exciting. It's another good football player at an important position."

McCarthy will be playing catch-up, taking a crash course in the Giants' offense with the hope that he can contribute sooner rather than later. For now, he'll back up Jameis Winston, who himself is still acclimating to his new position.

Winston was asked for his first impression of McCarthy, who was wearing jersey No. 18 on Wednesday.

"I think he's a good kid, and I'm happy to have anyone that's my teammate," Winston said after practice. "Obviously, we share -- we won the national championship. We share (that) he got coached by a Harbaugh. I'm getting coached by a Harbaugh right now. We share that -- those similarities. But he's curious. He wants to be great. I think anybody that gets the opportunity to come to a new organization with a fresh start wants to make an impact.

"What I want for myself, I want for everyone. So, if he wants to join the routine, he's definitely welcome."

Harbaugh said Winston would be the starter until further notice.

Winston, an 11-year NFL veteran, knows things can change quickly. He said he needs to play his best to stay in the role.

The Giants host the Arizona Cardinals this Sunday at MetLife Stadium. Winston will get the start, but many eyes will be on this situation over the next few weeks.

title: Pennsylvania reports its 5th measles-related death of the year amid outbreak
description: A Parkside Pediatrics provider assessing a patient with measles symptoms in Spartanburg, South Carolina, on 30 January 2026.Photograph: The Washington Post/Getty...
fullText:
Pennsylvania has reported its fifth measles-associated death of 2026 as the state's ongoing outbreak climbs to 943 confirmed cases across 39 counties.

The Pennsylvania department of health said on Wednesday that an unvaccinated Lancaster county resident who tested positive for measles had died. Health officials did not release further information about the individual, citing privacy protections.

The death marks the fifth Pennsylvania resident to meet the state's definition of a measles-associated death this year after a fourth death two weeks ago. Due to how the Trump administration has changed its method for reporting measles deaths, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has not counted the Pennsylvania measles deaths in its national tally.

As of Monday 28 September, Pennsylvania had recorded 40 new positive cases. The outbreak has now reached 39 counties, with 943 cumulative confirmed cases, 176 hospitalizations and five confirmed measles-associated deaths.

Only four of those confirmed cases have involved vaccinated individuals, representing less than 1% of the state's total cases.

Health officials say daily totals can change, but monitoring the numbers gives residents and healthcare providers a clearer picture of community transmission across Pennsylvania and helps guide the state's response.

Agricultural communities in Lancaster and Mifflin counties have remained at the center of Pennsylvania's outbreak. Utah, Florida, Virginia and Texas have also reported dozens of cases, according to tracking from Johns Hopkins University.

Since the outbreak began in late April, staff at state health centers have administered more than 5,500 measles, mumps and rubella vaccine (MMR) vaccinations through 180 pop-up vaccination clinics in affected communities, according to a statement released on Wednesday.

Dozens of additional vaccination clinics are planned for the coming weeks and months, depending on community interest and need, the statement added.

More than 3,600 measles cases have been reported across the US in 2026, according to the CDC. The US eliminated measles in 2000, though it is unclear whether it can retain that status amid the recent outbreaks.

Measles is considered one of the most contagious diseases known to medicine. The MMR vaccine prevents 97% of measles cases.

Vaccination rates among kindergarten-aged children, which are considered an important indicator, have slowly declined as experts argue the Trump administration is promoting confusion and misinformation about vaccines among parents.

Earlier this month, Pennsylvania requested emergency assistance from the CDC in response to the measles outbreak, but warned that the request could be withdrawn unless the federal agency publicly recognized the measles-associated deaths reported by the state.

The dispute began after Robert F Kennedy Jr, the US health secretary and former head of an anti-vaccine advocacy group, publicly questioned whether the deaths linked to the measles outbreaks since he took office were caused by the virus or by another condition.

A man accused of plotting a "violent attack" on the Texas Capitol in Austin is in custody after state authorities say they received a tip about the alleged threat and worked through the night to track down a suspect.

The Texas State Department of Public Safety and the FBI thwarted a "credible threat" against the state capitol, according to a notice sent to Texas state senators Wednesday and reviewed by ABC News. The alleged attack was to occur on Thursday, according to the notice and Texas DPS.

Texas DPS said it learned of the threat Tuesday evening. Special agents worked alongside the FBI and local partners before arresting 40-year-old Benny Caldera Jr., whom it called the "main suspect," at his residence in Converse, Texas, at around 3 a.m. Wednesday.

Caldera was transported to the Bexar County jail and has been charged with felony terroristic threat against a public servant, according to Texas DPS.

According to an official briefed on the investigation, the suspect had allegedly been threatening to conduct a mass shooting at the Texas Capitol on Thursday and had been collecting ammo and had guns.

Authorities were notified by people who knew the man that he has been growing more angry and potentially violent recently, the official said. Neither Caldera nor his wife are cooperating with the probe at this point, the official said, but other family members and co-workers are talking to investigators.

In recent weeks, the suspect had voiced anger over the state and direction of the country and the Palestinian cause, among other things, the official said. He also allegedly had been doing drugs more heavily.

Investigators are working to obtain search warrants for the suspect's devices to determine if he had any accomplices or co-conspirators and what significance Thursday's date has, according to the official.

FBI Director Kash Patel commended the investigation, calling the work of Texas DPS "outstanding."

"Threaten Americans or our institutions and law enforcement will move FAST," he said in a post on social media.

In the notice to state senators, Texas State Senate Secretary Patsy Spaw said the alleged threat was not cause for concern but that she wanted to let members know about it.

"The investigation is ongoing, and there is and will continue to be an enhanced DPS presence at the Capitol," Spaw wrote in the notice.

fullText:
Federal Communications Commission Chair Brendan Carr said Wednesday that new pro-Trump TV ads paid for with government funds don’t “merit any sort of FCC review.”

“It doesn’t strike me as anything at all out of the ordinary,” Carr said of the ads, which have aired across the country in recent weeks.

Asked about allegations that the ads are “propaganda,” Carr laughed.

The White House has “explained that these are just normal-course public service announcements, PSAs, that you see all the time. I don’t think there’s anything unique or different about it,” he said at a news conference.

“There’s nothing in there that strikes me that merit any sort of FCC review,” said Carr, whom Trump appointed to the agency.

A reporter pointed out that the progressive advocacy group Public Citizen filed a complaint with the FCC noting that the Trump campaign used one of the ads in 2024.

Carr brushed off the concern, telling reporters that “there’s groups on the left that have, you know, long worked and pushed to weaponize the FCC’s license renewal process” but that the ads “don’t raise any red flags.”

Public Citizen did not immediately respond to a request for comment Wednesday.

Anna Gomez, the lone Democratic commissioner on the FCC, told NBC News in a statement, “I recognize the concern shared by others that taxpayer dollars are being used to promote a political message, particularly given the timing of these ads coming so close to an election.”

“While it is not surprising to see the FCC exercise a double standard when it comes to its investigative decisions, I am certain we will hear more about this from folks in Congress, who are ultimately responsible,” her statement said.

The use of federal funds to pay for the ads has drawn bipartisan criticism, with Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., saying they “shouldn’t be paid for with taxpayer dollars” and Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., calling them an “absolute violation of what democracy is supposed to look like.”

Trump defended the ads when asked about them Wednesday in the Oval Office.

“I’m not running for office and I don’t talk about anybody,” he said. “When I’m talking about making America great, making our country great, that’s a countrywide ad. That’s an ad for the spirit of our country.”

“Now, if somebody said that that’s wrong, I’ll gladly pay the money. But these are ads for the country,” he added.

The first of the ads features Trump describing how he wants to “defeat communism” while the song “Love Me” by JMSN plays in the background.

Another spot is a slightly shorter version of a 2024 Trump campaign ad, which shows him walking down a hallway as he asks people in a voice-over to join him in his “final battle” to “demolish the deep state” and “expel the warmongers from our government.”

In its complaint Tuesday, Public Citizen said that the messages are thinly veiled campaign ads timed to motivate Trump’s supporters ahead of the upcoming midterm elections and that they are unlawful.

“Federal law explicitly prohibits using appropriated public funds for government propaganda, self-aggrandizement, or partisan political advertising. Yet, that is exactly the nature of Trump’s recent campaign ads,” the complaint says, adding that none of the ads to date “meet the standard of a public service announcement.”

“They do not refer to any specific governmental program and they do not serve the purpose of informing the public about any specific governmental program,” the complaint says.

Carr has made headlines for using his post to go after late-night comedians like Stephen Colbert and Jimmy Kimmel and network programs that he has alleged have liberal biases.

The FCC issued an order this year directing Disney’s eight owned-and-operated television stations to file their broadcast license renewals ahead of schedule after the White House and ABC clashed over a joke Kimmel made about first lady Melania Trump.

Disney is challenging the review with a suit alleging the FCC is seeking to coerce and retaliate against “a network that refuses to bow to the ⁠administration’s ​demands.” Carr has said the ABC license review stems from the FCC’s probe of Disney’s diversity, equity and inclusion practices — not “speech.”

title: White House removes CNN from press pool for Trump's upcoming trip to Texas and Oklahoma
description: President Donald Trump speaks to the media aboard Air Force One on its way to Joint Base Andrews, Md., from Ireland on Sept. 13.
fullText:
The White House on Wednesday removed CNN from the press pool that’s set to cover a trip by President Donald Trump on Thursday, escalating a feud with the cable network after a federal judge blocked the administration’s push to restrict its media access.

CNN had been designated to travel with Trump on Thursday, according to a press rotation document the White House released Sunday. But when the daily guidance came out for his scheduled visit to a truck manufacturing facility in Denton, Texas, followed by remarks in Durant, Oklahoma, it did not list CNN as providing pool coverage.

The move comes less than a week after a federal judge halted Trump’s effort to ban CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House. It also comes after the White House barred CNN from flying on Air Force One over the weekend when Trump traveled to Tennessee, when the network was scheduled to provide pool coverage. (The judge’s order was limited to media access on the White House grounds.)

Emily Kuhn, a spokesperson for CNN, confirmed the cable network’s removal from planned pool coverage but did not provide additional comment. Instead, she pointed to an earlier statement from Theodore Boutrous, an attorney representing CNN, MS NOW and Politico in their fight with the White House over press access.

“As we have said from the beginning, the President’s ban of CNN, MS NOW and POLITICO from the White House is a blatant violation of the First Amendment and due process,” Boutrous said in a statement Monday, when the three news outlets asked a federal judge to extend his pause on Trump’s ban.

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment about CNN’s exclusion from Thursday’s trip.

The White House press pool is a group of media outlets that share video, editorial information and costs for coverage of high-profile officials and events involving the president anywhere in the world. Under the system, each day’s designated “poolers” represent the wider press corps to document newsworthy events and serve as a conduit between the president and the public.

The White House Correspondents’ Association, the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press and a group of 49 news and media organizations that included NBCUniversal Media, the parent company of NBC News, filed a legal brief last week in support of CNN, MS NOW and Politico.

Other member networks of the pool — Fox News, ABC News, CBS News and NBC News — briefly boycotted participating in pool duties last week in solidarity with CNN.

NBC News did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the exclusion of CNN for Thursday’s trip and whether it intended to take any action.

Trump has restricted access for other news outlets before. In 2025, he banned The Associated Press from the Oval Office, Air Force One and certain events for not referring to the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America — his preferred name for the gulf.

The AP sued, and the case continues.

title: California bans child marriage, a practice still legal in 32 U.S. states
description: Brittany Bee was wed to a man when she was a teen. ...
fullText:
California has officially banned child marriage, with Governor Gavin Newsom signing legislation to end the practice that is still legal in 32 US states.

The new law, which will come into effect on 1 January, states people must be 18 to get married in the Golden State.

Newsom called it a "long overdue measure to protect young Californians and minors". He signed the bill into law with Courtney Stodden, whose parents allowed her to marry a 50-year-old Hollywood actor when she was just 16.

Stodden, who has been advocating to end the practice, called the change a "victory" and said survivors of child marriage should "never have been expected to carry this burden".

Stodden said she would "keep fighting until children are protected from marriage in all 50 states".

She was married to actor Doug Hutchison - known for roles in The Green Mile, A Time to Kill and I Am Sam - in 2011, spurring headlines internationally over the controversy and appearances on several reality programmes in the US, including the VH1 series Couples Therapy.

Other survivors of child marriage also applauded the new law.

"California has sent a clear message to the world today," Brittany Bee, a former child bride, told the BBC. "A message of hope for all children that they may be free from systemic violence. That they may choose their own path."

Bee told the BBC she was wed at the age of 17 to escape an abusive home - only to then be allegedly abused by her adult husband.

"I was just going from one prison to another," she explained. "People have the audacity to tell me that I made a choice - kids, they can't consent."

Bee and other child marriage survivors have been working for years to have child marriages banned in California and across the United States.

About a decade ago, the practice was still allowed across all US state but more and more states have been altering laws. California is the 18th to ban it since 2018.

In the state, there had been no legal age to wed, allowing children to get married as long as their parents consent and a judge signs off on the nuptials.

There was also no mechanism for people under 18 to get divorced and many girls say they were trapped in abusive and predatory relationships.

Unchained At Last, an advocacy group fighting to end child marriage across the US, said about 9,000 girls were wed each year in California and that almost all child marriages involved girls to adult men.

Advocates say that many in the US don't even know that child marriage is legal in so many US states, nor that is has led to allegations of abuse.

Sara Tasneem, who says she was forced to marry a man nearly twice her age when she was 15 years old, told the BBC that it felt "surreal" to finally have the state recognise that child marriage should be banned. She says she started lobbying for this herself in 2017.

She was introduced to her husband the morning of their arranged marriage.

"I was forced to be his wife and that day, my entire life changed," she told the BBC. She became a mother the following year, at the age of 16, and dropped out of school.

"To have seen the arc of this bill come to fruition has been a marathon," Tasneem said. "I'm just grateful that kids cannot get married after January 1, 2027 in California."

fullText:
Billy Joel doesn’t want anyone fretting too much over his health. The artist stepped away from performing last year after being diagnosed with normal pressure hydrocephalus, a brain disorder caused by an excessive accumulation of cerebrospinal fluid in the brain’s ventricles. Still, he doesn’t think it’s a big deal.

“I know people are worried about me because they read that I have a brain disorder, which sounds a lot worse than it actually is,” Joel recently shared on SiriusXM while taking calls from fans. “I’m okay. My balance isn’t that good. Lost a little bit of my hearing, but that may have to do with my age, too, and the rock and roll life and the loud volume probably didn’t help. But I’m fine. I want people to not have to worry about me. I’m okay.”

After initially refusing surgical intervention, Joel had a shunt implanted to alleviate some effects of the disorder. The procedure has helped to improve his memory, balance, and overall function, he shared earlier this month.

Joel still isn’t sure when he will return to the stage — beyond the surprise appearance he made with a cover band earlier this year — but this absence of performances has been referred to as a “recovery period” in recent statements from his team. “This condition has been exacerbated by recent concert performances, leading to problems with hearing, vision, and balance,” his team said last year. “Under his doctor’s instructions, Billy is undergoing specific physical therapy and has been advised to refrain from performing.”

For his part, at 77 years old, Joel can’t entirely tell which health hiccups are a result of his age versus the disorder. “They don’t want me to stress too much,” Joel said about his medical team. He doesn’t want anyone else stressing too much, either.

title: Flydubai pilot hailed a hero after fighting off attacker as plane plunged
description:
Indian pilot Smit Machchhar has been hailed as a hero for saving passengers after he was stabbed by his colleague in an alleged attempt to crash a Flydubai plane on Wednesday. - Israel Foreign Ministry/Reuters
The Indian pilot who fought off a savage attack by his copilot and helped prevent an apparent hijack of a Flydubai plane heading to Israel with more than 170 people on board is being hailed as a hero.
Captain Smit Machchhar was stabbed while trying to fend off the attacker, leaving him badly wounded. During the struggle the cockpit door was opened, allowing other passengers to rush in, subdue his assailant, and take control of the plane that was enroute to Tel Aviv.
Machchhar’s actions have received widespread praise from political leaders, passengers who were onboard, those who know him as well as strangers who gathered in his home town to celebrate his bravery.
fullText:
The Indian pilot who fought off a savage attack by his copilot and helped prevent an apparent hijack of a Flydubai plane heading to Israel with more than 170 people on board is being hailed as a hero.

Captain Smit Machchhar was stabbed while trying to fend off the attacker, leaving him badly wounded. During the struggle the cockpit door was opened, allowing other passengers to rush in, subdue his assailant, and take control of the plane that was enroute to Tel Aviv.

Machchhar’s actions have received widespread praise from political leaders, passengers who were onboard, those who know him as well as strangers who gathered in his home town to celebrate his bravery.

Kaushik Gandhi, who lives in the same building as Machchhar’s parents, told CNN the pilot was always smiling and happy, a real “gentleman.”

He described Machchhar as “first class” and said he would always say hello when visiting.

“Our entire India should be proud … he has brought glory to India’s name everywhere in the world,” Gandhi told CNN, adding he was “thumping (his) chest” in pride.

A crowd of supporters have also gathered in Ghatkopar East, the eastern Mumbai suburb where Machchhar’s family lives. They were waving Indian flags and photos of the hero pilot.

“It is a very precious moment and proud moment for a country like us that we have been through, you know, lot of hustles,” Rahul Pandey, one of those gathered there, told CNN.

“Smit Machchhar is a talented, soft spoken, kind-hearted and a person with good nature,” said Jinat Shah, who used to live next door to him in Mumbai before the pilot moved to Dubai. “He is an incredible person, and I hope for his fast recovery,” Shah told Indian news agency ANI.

Passengers who were on flight FZ1073 described those chaotic moments, during which the plane plummeted 17,400 feet in less than 120 seconds. One told CNN: “I was just sure I was going to die.”

But after the attacker was restrained, the flight was diverted to Saudi Arabia, where it was safely landed by two standby pilots who happened to be flying as passengers

Machchhar, who is reported to be a 39-year-old father of two, was seriously wounded in the attack.

Machchhar had suffered “massive blood loss” and was “severely wounded,” dentist Shota Musaev, a passenger on the flight who helped treat him, told CNN.

“I think that if we had waited even a few more moments, we would have lost him; his blood pressure had plummeted, he suddenly lost consciousness, and there was blood everywhere,” he said.

His bravery “managed to prevent a 9/11 disaster,” Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told CNN.

Machchhar is receiving medical care at a hospital in Saudi Arabia, according to the Indian embassy in Riyadh, and is in stable condition.

Parag Shah, who represents Ghatkopar East, the eastern Mumbai suburb Machchhar is from, told CNN that the pilot was “out of danger” after undergoing surgery on Wednesday, citing family members.

Born into a family in the textile business, becoming a pilot wasn’t Machchhar’s “childhood dream,” he told the Bona-Fide Banter podcast in 2025.

Initially, he’d enrolled in a textile engineering course after school.

“I finished the entire course, I still was young so wanted to (do) a little more studies,” he said.

Once he decided on flying, training took him to New Zealand, where he arrived aged around 19, in the southern city of Dunedin.

“He was always sort of a jovial young man and he tried hard,” his instructor at the time Philip Kean told CNN.

In a group photograph Kean shared from those days, Machchhar is easy to pick out. “He definitely got a smile of his own… he’s sort of a happy, happy chap,” said Kean, CEO of Mainland Air in Dunedin.

Before joining Flydubai, Machchhar spent 11 years with Indian carrier SpiceJet, rising to the position of Senior Commander, according to his LinkedIn profile.

Before Wednesday’s incident, one of the most unusual situations he had faced during his over 15 years of flying was the birth of a baby on board.

A woman on the plane, who was not at term, had started experiencing labor pains, Machchhar told the Bona-Fide Banter podcast. “Within 7-10 minutes, she was like, ‘captain this is now advancing toward a delivery.’”

Machchhar said he and the first officer started to check for the nearest airfields and conditions to make a safe landing. “Both the mother baby were fine,” he added.

Watching the news of Machchhar’s heroic actions on the Flydubai flight from New Zealand, his former instructor Kean was full of praise for the young man he had once taught.

“It was an amazing feat,” he told CNN.

“There could have been a whole airplane load of people wiped out in a matter of seconds, and luckily they got the door open… luckily he could hang on and save the day. Another half a minute would have been all over.”

“I’m very proud,” he said. “I’m very proud that he handled that situation… It’s great the way it turned out.”

Machchhar has become a national hero for two nations –– Israel, where most of the passengers hailed from, and his own home country, India.

“The pilot from Mumbai who proved to be a hero,” wrote the Times of India.

“Viewers, if 166 Israelis go home tonight without a scratch, it is all down to the bravery of one single Indian, Captain Smit Machchhar,” a CNN News-18 anchor said during his primetime program.

Speaking on the podcast last year how he felt to be a pilot, Machchhar’s answer was simple: “Blessed.”

Additional reporting by Sandi Sidhu.

title: NASA telescope could fall to Earth within weeks after daring rescue falls short
description:
NASA’s Swift Observatory orbits above Earth in an artist’s concept. - Goddard Space Flight Center/NASA

fullText:
A celebrated space telescope is rapidly dipping from its once-stable orbit and falling to Earth just shy of the 22nd anniversary of its launch.

The Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory will soon have to cease its science observations after a daring rescue mission’s attempt to boost its orbit failed over the summer.

Named after fast-flying birds, the telescope could quickly pivot to observe blink-and-you-miss-it cosmic events like flaring black holes. The telescope was originally designed to study the most powerful explosions in the universe, called gamma-ray bursts, but scientists have also used it to observe other types of cosmic flashes, as well as asteroids and comets.

The 3,200-pound (1,452-kilogram) observatory is currently located about 200 miles (325 kilometers) above Earth. But engineers estimate that once Swift drifts below 185 miles (300 kilometers) in early to mid-October, operating the telescope will become a challenge, according to NASA. Then, Swift will drop from orbit and is expected to burn up in Earth’s atmosphere during the plunge.

“While it’s possible some hardware from the Swift spacecraft may survive re-entry due to its size, the probability of debris causing significant property damage or physical harm to anyone is very small,” according to statement from space-tracking company LeoLabs shared with CNN via email. “More likely, as is the case with most debris that survives re-entry, it will fall into the ocean or on land that’s uninhabited.”

NASA didn’t respond to request for comment on the potential risks related to the observatory’s reentry.

Scientists hoped that a rapidly produced satellite called LINK, which was developed, built and launched by Arizona-based Katalyst Space Technologies in just nine months, could grapple the telescope and lift it into a stable orbit.

The rescue mission to boost Swift failed just a few weeks after launching LINK in early July as the satellite spun out of control in space.

“From the beginning, this was a high-risk, high-reward mission,” said Shawn Domagal-Goldman, Astrophysics Division director at NASA, in a statement. “Without intervention, Swift was going to re-enter the atmosphere by year’s end.”

But NASA and Katalyst say LINK’s modified mission was not a wasted effort, with both groups learning lessons that could aid future space operations.

“And while we’ll be sad to see Swift’s mission come to a close, we knew this boost effort would be valuable to the agency on multiple levels — advancing U.S. spacecraft servicing technology, challenging us to meet unprecedented mission timelines, and testing how we operate satellites to extend their time in low Earth orbit,” Domagal-Goldman further stated. “We’re very proud of how quickly this team got so far, and we’re capturing lessons learned to ensure we’re ready to go even farther.”

Katalyst decided to forge ahead with its plan for LINK to rendezvous with Swift in mid-August, but as a demonstration rather than a rescue because of LINK’s ongoing orientation issues in space.

While Katalyst’s engineers were able to use the satellite’s thrusters to slow its unexpected spin and upload new flight software, the maneuver that reoriented LINK in space also depleted its propellant.

“As a result, Katalyst and NASA together determined that LINK no longer had sufficient fuel to safely execute the planned capture and orbit-raising phase of the mission,” according to Katalyst.

The satellite came within 7.5 to 9 miles (12 to 15 kilometers) of Swift the first week of September, practicing how a future servicing mission may approach a satellite or telescope — especially one like Swift, which wasn’t designed to be serviced in space.

LINK also deployed its three robotic arms, which were originally intended to grab Swift, and fired its three electric propulsion thrusters.

The satellite operated in space for 85 days before reentering Earth’s atmosphere on September 25, according to Katalyst.

“LINK was built to take on a problem that did not have an easy solution,” said Ghonhee Lee, CEO of Katalyst Space. “While we did not accomplish every objective we set out to achieve, in less than a year we went from mission concept to launching and operating the first commercial space robot. This is a foundation we can build on.”

Katalyst will apply data and lessons from LINK’s mission to its next generation of spacecraft that could be used to service existing missions in space.

“The future of space will require spacecraft that can do more once they get there. We’re building toward that future,” Lee said.

The Swift Observatory, which does not have an established observational replacement waiting in the wings, has served as an astrophysics multitool in low-Earth orbit since it launched in November 2004.

Swift’s mission scientists have slowly been turning the telescope’s instruments back on to collect data and make observations right up until the end — which is actually accelerating the observatory’s decline.

The instruments were shut off for months to reduce power use and keep Swift from sinking.

Swift was steadily losing altitude due to atmospheric drag, which was only magnified by an increase in solar activity over the past couple of years as the sun reached the peak of its 11-year cycle in 2024.

Intense flares and coronal mass ejections caused Earth’s atmosphere to expand, which intensified the drag on Swift, leading scientists to predict it would descend toward our planet in the fall, according to NASA.

“When Neil Gehrels, Swift’s namesake, designed the observatory, nothing like it had ever launched,” said S. Bradley Cenko, Swift’s principal investigator at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland. “He would have celebrated that this boost effort was part of Swift’s legacy, that it allowed NASA to try something new and daring even though the outcome wasn’t guaranteed.”
